reference: BMW M5 Competition (F90, LCI), S63B44T4 4.4 L twin-turbo hot-V cross-plane V8 with cross-bank exhaust manifolds, valved M Sport exhaust, EU specification. Engineering reference only.

interior.source: research estimate of Car and Driver-comparable levels for the M5 Competition (C/D 2018 base M5: 74 dBA full throttle, 80 peak in Sport, 66 at 70 mph; auto motor und sport LCI Competition: idle 48, max 81, 69 at 100 km/h, 71 at 130 km/h)

exterior.source: BMW stationary noise via auto motor und sport; test speed from the UN R51.03 rule (estimate)

notes.engine.firingOrder: [P] 1-5-4-8-6-3-7-2, BMW technical training manual ST1202 (S63TU, F10 M5), table for S63 and S63TU; the F90's cross-bank manifold only works with this order, so carry-over to the S63B44T4 is near certain [A].
notes.engine.banks: [P] BMW numbering (ST1202): cylinder 1 at the front of the RIGHT bank (passenger side of a left-hand-drive car, looking forward); right bank 1-2-3-4 and left bank 5-6-7-8, front to rear. Per-bank pulse gaps 180-270-180-90 (right) and 180-90-180-270 (left): the classic cross-plane pattern.
notes.engine.crank: [P] Cross-plane forged crank, 5 main bearings (ST1202, S63TU), assumed carried over [A]. Even 90-degree firing.
notes.engine.idleRpm: [E] Not published; warm idle of the N63/S63 family 550-650 rpm (research). Matches the car config.
notes.engine.limiterRpm: [F] BMW NA (M5 CS, same engine): redline 7,200 rpm; [P] ST1202: cut-off speed 7,200 rpm. Matches the car config.
notes.exhaust.collectors: [P] Hot-V cross-bank manifolds (ST1202, kept on the F90 per BMW 2017/2020): the twin-scroll turbo over the left bank (5-8) takes cylinders 1/6 (front scroll) and 4/7 (rear scroll); the turbo over the right bank (1-4) takes 2/8 (front) and 3/5 (rear). Each scroll gets a pulse every 360 degrees (BMW: '360 degrees of crankshaft angle between the two exhaust cycles within the exhaust flute'), each turbo every 180 degrees, the two turbos 90 degrees apart. [E] Primary lengths: short hot-V runners, about 0.3 m from the near bank to 0.5 m crossing the V; 0.40 m mean with 0.05 m spread.
notes.exhaust.gasTempK: [E] About 1,150 K ahead of close-coupled turbines at full load (gasoline turbo).
notes.exhaust.pipeTempK: [E] About 750 K after the turbines and close-coupled catalysts.
notes.exhaust.rasp: [E] Lower than the shared default 0.35: the turbines take the sharp part out of the pulses and reviewers call the stock note smooth and 'mellow' from inside.
notes.exhaust.merge: [F] Dual-branch M Sport exhaust, one branch per turbo, with a Helmholtz resonator between the two rear silencers (BMW NA 2018). [E] The shared resonator modelled as a weak low-frequency coupling (an H-pipe, 12 % below about 250 Hz).
notes.exhaust.outlets: [F] Four tailpipes, two per side (one branch per side). [E] About 3.45 m of pipe from each turbo in the V to its rear silencer, mirror-image branches of equal length, 0.25 m tails, 76 mm pipes; the far branch 0.1 m further from the listener (about the path difference at the driver's seat). The two branches carry the turbos' 180-degree pulse trains 90 degrees apart, so their orders 2 and 6 largely cancel when both are heard equally: measured with unequal branches (3.4 / 3.5 m, 0.2 m offset) order 2 rose to +5 dB over the firing order at 7,200 rpm near the pipes' third resonance (about 235 Hz), against the research's 'orders 4 and 8 dominate, weaker 2 and 6'.
notes.exhaust.muffler: [F] Electrically actuated flaps following EFFICIENT / SPORT / SPORT+ (M Sound Control forces the quiet setting). [E] This is SPORT, the game's default: open under load (above 50 % load) and above 3,500 rpm; filter values are the shared defaults.
notes.intake.level: [E] Front engine with the intakes outside the V, far from the cabin; turbo compressors and water-to-air charge cooling muffle the induction.
notes.intake.runnerLengthM: [E] Short runners on the outside of the hot-V.
notes.mechanical: [E] Shared calibrated defaults; injector ticks a little above default for 350-bar direct injection [F].
notes.idle: [E] No big-cam lope (VALVETRONIC and Double-VANOS [F]); shared default roughness.
notes.overrun.burble: [E] SPORT: occasional light burble on lift-off (research); SPORT+ would be about 0.3. EU cars have a particulate filter [F], which softens crackle [E].
notes.forcedInduction.pulseDamping: [E] Twin-scroll turbines inside the V smooth the pulses a little more than the shared default.
notes.forcedInduction.whistleHz: [E] Subdued whistle on the stock car (research); pitch range kept in the audible band.
notes.forcedInduction.whistleLevel: [E] Below the shared default 0.10: subdued whistle.
notes.forcedInduction.blowOff: [P] No blow-off valve: BMW (ST1202): the S63TU 'does not use a blow-off valve. The use of Valvetronic and special tuning rendered it unnecessary'; compressors 'not sensitive to pump'. Carry-over assumed [A]. variants 0 makes no blow-off sounds.
notes.limiter.type: [E] Cut style not published (fuel or ignition cut); a fuel cut without afterfire pops.
notes.limiter.rpm: [F] 7,200 rpm (see engine.limiterRpm). In manual the gearbox doesn't upshift at the limiter, so the engine bounces on it [F]; in D it upshifts just before.
notes.limiter.free: [E] Research suggests a 10-15 Hz bounce of 150-250 rpm; free revving bounces faster and deeper (14 Hz, 250 rpm).
notes.limiter.load: [E] In gear, 10 Hz and 150 rpm (the car's inertia holds the engine up).
notes.loops.rpmPoints: [E] Idle to the limiter, about 1.33 x apart (the shared default spacing).
notes.loudness.interior: [E] Research estimate for Car and Driver-comparable figures (gap: C/D's Competition levels weren't found): idle 47, full throttle 79, 67 dBA at 70 mph. Corroborated by auto motor und sport's measured LCI Competition (idle 48, max 81) [M]. These cabin levels include BMW Active Sound Design, which in SPORT adds at most about 6 dB at full throttle [E] (C/D: 74 dBA, 80 peak in Sport, base M5). The cruise figure is road, wind and engine together; the level model uses idle and full throttle only.
notes.loudness.exterior: [F] 86 dBA stationary (BMW via auto motor und sport); [E] at 3,750 rpm (UN R51.03 rule for engines rated at 5,000-7,500 rpm, to verify). For reference; not used by the level model.
